purpose: Peak resident bytes while streaming a real checkpoint, measured against a resident ceiling C that is configured independently of the measurement. Committed so the numbers stay auditable after models/ (gitignored) is deleted and after this machine is gone.
why_the_ceiling_is_not_derived_from_the_: QM-0100 reported peak RSS 3473408 B and derived C = R/1.25, which makes 'peak <= 1.25 x C' an identity that cannot fail. Its independent reviewer ruled that honest but near-tautological and explicitly not a G1 pass. Every ceiling below is instead declared in a file checked into this repository before any run: see each row's `ceiling_declared_in`. The row labelled g1-ceiling-breached-by-mmap exists to prove the comparison is falsifiable, by showing the SAME ceiling being exceeded 75.07x by a real configuration of the same binary.

measured_on.machine: Apple M3 Pro, 36 GB unified memory (.plan/MASTER_PLAN.md §4's development machine)
measured_on.commit: recorded in .plan/evidence/QM-0101.md `## Merge`; this branch is task/qm-0101-bounded-residency-proof off base d49701c

binary_note: The binary is `q`, not `q-cli`: crates/q-cli/Cargo.toml declares [[bin]] name = "q". QM-0100 recorded the same discrepancy against its own task file.
measurement_method: /usr/bin/time -l <binary> stream <dir> --resident-ceiling <C> --io <mode>, reading the `maximum resident set size` line. macOS reports that field in BYTES. The measuring program is outside this repository, so nothing in this workspace can influence what it reports.
peak_rss_label_reason: RSS is sampled by the kernel and includes the binary's text, its thread stacks, and the allocator's arenas as well as the pass's own buffers. The EXACT heap figure for the same pass comes from the counting allocator in tests/tests/residency_peak_allocation.rs and is 1053015 / 1102726 / 1084769 B for the three checkpoint sizes; the two are different metrics and neither is presented as the other.
runs_per_row: 12 or more; each row records its own `sample_size` and `observed_peak_range_bytes`
reported_run: For a row that claims the ceiling HOLDS, the largest observed peak. For the row that claims the ceiling is BREACHED, the smallest. Both are the conservative direction for the claim the row makes, so neither is the flattering end of its own range.
tolerance_note: 1.25 x C, from .plan/MASTER_PLAN.md §4. Computed as an exact integer ratio by q_source::budget::resident_tolerance_bytes, never in floating point. It is a tolerance on the MEASUREMENT: a configuration is admitted against C itself, so the 25 % is never spent twice.
flatness_span_note: 352824413 / 105912. The three `flatness_series` rows share one ceiling and the largest observed peak moves by 1.306x across that span (2949120 B to 3850240 B). V1-05's third, >= 24 GB size does not exist on this machine.

rows.label: g1-headline
rows.ceiling_declared_in: .plan/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md V1-04: "Against 352,824,413 bytes, N >= 100 requires C <= ~3.4 MB". C = floor(352824413 / 100), derived from the checkpoint size, which was known before any pass ran.
rows.peak_memory_footprint_note: macOS's phys_footprint. Reported because it excludes clean file-backed pages and so isolates the process's own memory; NOT the metric TASK.md names, and not the one the verdict rests on.
rows.accounted_resident_formula: (min(max_output_queue_depth, max_concurrent_blocks) + 2) x block_rows x block_columns x 4 + block_columns x 8 = (4 + 2) x 256 x 256 x 4 + 256 x 8
rows.peak_reported: largest observed — the conservative direction for a claim that the ceiling holds

rows.label: g1-ceiling-breached-by-mmap
rows.ceiling_declared_in: the same .plan/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md V1-04 ceiling as g1-headline — deliberately identical, so this row measures that ceiling rather than a different one
rows.why_it_exceeds: Memory-mapped pages count toward RSS while they are resident (.plan/MEMORY_BUDGET.md §3). On a machine under no memory pressure the kernel has no reason to evict them, so a mapped pass over a 337 MiB checkpoint reports approximately the file in its peak RSS even though the pass holds 1574912 B of buffers. Note the identical checksum and byte count: this is the SAME work, measured on the same ceiling, failing. TASK.md's Risks table anticipated exactly this and forbade redefining the metric to pass; the answer taken instead was to stop mapping in the streaming path.
rows.peak_reported: smallest observed — the conservative direction for a claim that the ceiling is breached

rows.n_verdict: N = 0.1643 does NOT reach 100. The ceiling holds with 697x of room, and that is exactly why this row cannot carry G1: a 337 MiB checkpoint is not 100 x 2 GiB. Reaching N >= 100 at C = 2 GiB needs a checkpoint of at least 200 GiB.

refusal_accounting.note: A real checkpoint is mostly not rank-2, and ADR-010 requires rank above 3 to be refused rather than flattened. The refused tensors are counted and their bytes reconciled rather than silently skipped, so 'every byte of every streamable tensor, exactly once' is a checked claim.

determinism.note: The fold is position-sensitive and order-independent, so the same total must appear whatever grid the tensors were cut into. 64x64 over the real checkpoint gives 19992 blocks against 1251 at 256x256 and the identical checksum 0x75cb70c1b672895d.
determinism.interrupted_plus_resumed_evidence: --stop-after-blocks 100 gives 26214400 B and 0x07b895126626ad11; --resume-from-block 100 gives 301190144 B and 0x6e12dbaf504bdc4c; the sums are 327404544 B and 0x75cb70c1b672895d, exactly the uninterrupted pass.

g1_verdict.ceiling_declared_in: .plan/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md V1-04, applied to fixtures/real-checkpoint-record.json's measured 352824413 bytes

conjuncts.evidence: C = 3528244 B = 3.365 MiB, which is 608.7x under 2 GiB
largest of 20 release runs, 3850240 B <= 4410305 B, measured by /usr/bin/time -l. Observed range 3522560..3850240 B; every run in the sample cleared the tolerance.

true_by_construction: N >= 100 is arithmetic, not a measurement: C was chosen as floor(checkpoint_bytes / 100), so N = 100 holds by construction at this ceiling. What the measurement decides is the third conjunct, peak <= 1.25 x C, and that comparison is falsifiable — the g1-ceiling-breached-by-mmap row shows the same ceiling being exceeded 75x.
measured_and_falsifiable: peak <= 1.25 x C. Demonstrated failing twice: once at the measurement level (g1-ceiling-breached-by-mmap, smallest of 13 runs 331038720 B against a 4410305 B tolerance, 75.07x over, with not one run of that configuration inside the tolerance) and once at the admission level (`--resident-ceiling 1MiB` exits 1 with `memory budget exceeded [max_resident]: requested 1574912 bytes, limit 1048576 bytes`).
g1_verdict.what_the_pass_does_not_cover: 56 of 82 tensors are refused rather than streamed, correctly, under ADR-010. 92.8 % of the described payload streams. TASK.md acceptance criterion 1 as written — 'the full checkpoint streams' — is therefore PARTIALLY met and is recorded as such in .plan/evidence/QM-0101.md.
g1_verdict.measured_peak_note: largest of 20 release runs at this ceiling; the observed range was 3522560..3850240 B

coverage_not_established: >= 24 GB scale. This checkpoint is 352824413 bytes (~337 MiB), about 1/70th of the 24 GB .plan/MASTER_PLAN.md §4 originally wanted. The owner re-scoped to it in 579107f and .plan/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md V1-01 records the re-scope. G1 is established at C = 3.365 MiB on a 337 MiB file, NOT at C <= 2 GB on a >= 24 GB file. crates/q-catalog/tests/trillion_scale_manifest.rs is metadata-only and may never substitute for this.
The sharded read path at scale. models/distilbert-distilgpt2 is a single file with no model.safetensors.index.json. Multi-shard streaming is measured only over fixtures/tiny-llama-2shard, at 1.2 MB.

Throughput. Elapsed seconds are recorded because they were observed, not because they were measured under controlled conditions: the page cache was warm, no run was repeated cold, and nothing was pinned. QM-0102 owns throughput. A residency measurement says nothing about how fast the bytes moved.
GPU, device memory, and deployment. No CUDA or Metal code runs in this pass. q-cuda remains Hardware-Unverified. Nothing here is a claim about any device, any deployment, or any partner.

mmap page-level residency. The g1-ceiling-breached-by-mmap row shows that mapped pages inflate RSS, but no vmmap or mincore measurement of which pages were resident when was taken. The mapped read path's page-level behaviour remains unmeasured, and the G1 figure covers the pread path only: q value, q slice, and q stats still map and do not inherit this bound.

Rank-1 and rank-3 visualization. 50 rank-1 tensors are refused because BlockExtent is 2-D; ADR-010's designed rank-1 and rank-3 bindings are QM-0061's and QM-0040's work and are not implemented. The 6 rank-4 masks are refused by design and always will be.
bf16 exact decode on real data. All 82 tensors are F32. The bf16 and f16 paths are exercised only by fixtures.
Semantic meaning. The checksum proves bytes were read. It says nothing about what any weight means, and no role was resolved in this pass.

exact_heap_flatness.sensitivity_check: the same pass at 512x512 blocks peaks at 4248454 B — 3.9x the 256x256 figure — so the measurement does track the configured block size and its flatness result is not a fixed floor
exact_heap_flatness.why_it_matters: RSS at these magnitudes is dominated by the binary's own text, so RSS flatness across sizes is nearly uninformative. This figure is the one that carries V1-05; the RSS rows corroborate it.
exact_heap_flatness.spread_definition: max - min over every measured phase, the stricter of the two definitions: a middle phase that spiked would slip past a smallest-vs-largest comparison.
exact_heap_flatness.determinism: Four consecutive runs produced byte-identical figures. This is a counting allocator over a deterministic pass, so it is EXACT and reproducible, unlike the RSS rows which the kernel samples.

rss_variance_note: Peak RSS moves by tens of kilobytes between otherwise identical runs — the kernel samples it, and it includes the allocator's arenas. That is why every row records a range and a sample size rather than one number, and why the EXACT figure (see `exact_heap_flatness`) is the one that carries flatness. The three release runs QM-0100 reported showed the same order of variance.
